points.title: 童年岁月
points.description: 1795年10月31日，约翰·济慈出生于伦敦一个马厩主家庭。他是家中长子，随后还有三个弟妹。济慈的父亲托马斯·济慈是马厩主，母亲弗朗西斯·詹宁斯出身于富裕家庭。1800年，济慈的父亲因坠马去世，家庭陷入经济困境。济慈的舅舅理查德·詹宁斯接管了家庭，并安排济慈进入恩菲尔德的一所优秀学校接受教育。这段时期，济慈对古典文学产生了浓厚兴趣，尤其是荷马和维吉尔的史诗。
points.descriptionEn: John Keats was born on October 31, 1795, in London to the family of a stable keeper. He was the eldest of four children. His father Thomas Keats died in 1800 after falling from a horse, plunging the family into financial difficulties. Keats' uncle Richard Jennings took over the family and arranged for him to attend a good school in Enfield. During this period, Keats developed a strong interest in classical literature, particularly the epics of Homer and Virgil.

points.title: 医学学徒
points.description: 1811年，16岁的济慈成为外科医生托马斯·哈蒙德的学徒，开始了医学训练。1814年，他进入盖伊医院学习外科和药剂学，成为一名合格的药剂师。然而，济慈对医学的热情逐渐被文学创作所取代。他在医院期间开始写诗，并受到朋友查尔斯·克莱尔的影响，对诗歌产生了更深的兴趣。1815年，他决定放弃医学事业，全心投入诗歌创作，这一决定虽然遭到家人反对，但坚定了他的文学道路。
points.descriptionEn: In 1811, at age 16, Keats became an apprentice to surgeon Thomas Hammond, beginning his medical training. In 1814, he entered Guy's Hospital to study surgery and pharmacy, becoming a qualified apothecary. However, Keats' enthusiasm for medicine gradually gave way to literary creation. He began writing poetry during his time at the hospital and was influenced by his friend Charles Clarke, developing a deeper interest in poetry. In 1815, he decided to abandon medicine and devote himself entirely to poetry, a decision that was opposed by his family but solidified his literary path.

points.title: 诗歌创作高峰
points.description: 1816年是济慈诗歌生涯的转折点，他的第一首诗《哦，孤独！》发表在《观察家》杂志上。1817年，他出版第一本诗集《诗歌》，但反响平平。1818年，济慈创作了《恩底弥翁》，这是一部关于牧羊人爱上月神的叙事长诗，虽然评论褒贬不一，但展示了他的诗歌才华。1819年被认为是济慈的'奇迹年'，他创作了《夜莺颂》、《希腊古瓮颂》、《秋颂》等不朽名篇，以及《圣艾格尼丝之夜》等叙事诗。这一时期，济慈与雪莱、拜伦等浪漫主义诗人交往，形成了独特的诗歌风格，以丰富的感官意象和对美的追求著称。
points.descriptionEn: 1816 marked a turning point in Keats' poetic career when his first poem 'O Solitude!' was published in The Examiner. In 1817, he published his first collection, Poems, which received a lukewarm reception. In 1818, Keats wrote Endymion, a narrative poem about a shepherd's love for the moon goddess, which received mixed reviews but showcased his poetic talent. 1819 is considered Keats' 'annus mirabilis' when he wrote immortal works such as 'Ode to a Nightingale,' 'Ode on a Grecian Urn,' and 'To Autumn,' as well as narrative poems like 'The Eve of St. Agnes.' During this period, Keats associated with Romantic poets like Shelley and Byron, developing a unique poetic style characterized by rich sensory imagery and a pursuit of beauty.

points.title: 病逝异乡
points.description: 1820年，济慈的健康状况急剧恶化，被诊断出患有肺结核。在医生和朋友们的建议下，他于9月前往意大利寻求更好的气候条件。济慈于1821年2月23日在罗马逝世，年仅25岁。临终前，他要求墓碑上只刻下'此地长眠者，姓名写在水上'，拒绝提及自己的文学成就。济慈的早逝使英国文学界失去了一位极具天赋的诗人，他的作品在他生前并未获得广泛认可，直到维多利亚时期才被重新发现并高度评价。罗马的英国公墓成为他最后的安息之地，如今已成为文学朝圣者的目的地。
points.descriptionEn: In 1820, Keats' health deteriorated rapidly, and he was diagnosed with tuberculosis. On the advice of doctors and friends, he traveled to Italy in September seeking a better climate. Keats died in Rome on February 23, 1821, at the age of 25. On his deathbed, he requested that his tombstone bear only the words 'Here lies one whose name was writ in water,' refusing to mention his literary achievements. Keats' early death deprived the British literary world of an exceptionally talented poet. His works were not widely recognized during his lifetime but were rediscovered and highly valued during the Victorian era. The English Cemetery in Rome became his final resting place and is now a destination for literary pilgrims.

points.title: 爱情与友谊
points.description: 1818年至1819年间，济慈在伦敦汉普斯特德地区度过了一段重要的时光。他在此地与范妮·布朗相爱，两人于1819年订婚。范妮成为济慈灵感的源泉，他的许多情诗都受到这段感情的影响。同时，济慈与诗人查尔斯·布朗同住在温特沃斯小屋，这段友谊对他的创作产生了重要影响。汉普斯特德的乡村环境为济慈提供了宁静的创作空间，使他能够专注于诗歌创作。正是在这里，济慈完成了他最著名的作品，包括《夜莺颂》和《希腊古瓮颂》。然而，这段时期也伴随着济慈健康状况的恶化和经济困境，为他的早逝埋下了伏笔。
points.descriptionEn: Between 1818 and 1819, Keats spent a significant period in Hampstead, London. He fell in love with Fanny Brawne here, and they became engaged in 1819. Fanny became a source of inspiration for Keats, and many of his love poems were influenced by this relationship. Simultaneously, Keats lived with poet Charles Brown in Wentworth Place, a friendship that significantly impacted his work. Hampstead's rural environment provided Keats with a peaceful space for creation, where he completed some of his most famous works, including 'Ode to a Nightingale' and 'Ode on a Grecian Urn.' However, this period was also marked by Keats' deteriorating health and financial difficulties, foreshadowing his early death.

appraisal.zh: 济慈被公认为英国浪漫主义诗歌的巅峰代表之一，其颂歌已成英语文学经典，对美的极致追求与感官丰富性深刻影响了丁尼生、叶芝和艾略特，"消极能力"之说亦被视为现代诗歌的重要贡献；他早逝于罗马、墓碑铭文"姓名写在水上"，更使其生平成为文学浪漫主义的象征。也有研究者指出，他的诗时有感伤与自我沉溺之弊，偏重个人情感而社会关怀不足，形式上偶显松散，对古典的模仿亦嫌刻意。但这类意见终究不能动摇其以短暂生命达成的艺术成就与深远影响。
appraisal.en: Keats is widely regarded as one of the pinnacles of British Romantic poetry; his odes are classics of English literature, and his pursuit of beauty and sensory richness deeply influenced Tennyson, Yeats and Eliot, while his notion of 'negative capability' is counted a significant contribution to modern poetry. His early death in Rome and the epitaph 'name writ in water' have made his life a symbol of literary romanticism. Yet some researchers note tendencies toward sentimentality and self-indulgence, scant social concern, occasional structural looseness and deliberate imitation of the classics. Such reservations do not diminish the achievement of his brief life or his lasting influence.

supporter.zh: 济慈被赞誉为英国浪漫主义诗歌的巅峰代表之一，他的作品展现了对美的极致追求和深刻的情感体验。支持者认为济慈通过诗歌超越了个人痛苦，将短暂的生命转化为永恒的艺术。他的'消极能力'理论——能够忍受不确定性而不急于寻求答案——被视为现代诗歌的重要贡献。济慈对自然、艺术和爱情的敏锐感知，以及他诗歌中的感官丰富性，使他成为后世诗人如丁尼生、叶芝和艾略特的重要影响源。
supporter.en: Keats is celebrated as one of the pinnacle representatives of British Romantic poetry, whose works demonstrate an ultimate pursuit of beauty and profound emotional experience. Supporters believe that Keats transcended personal suffering through poetry, transforming his brief life into eternal art. His concept of 'negative capability'—the ability to endure uncertainty without rushing to find answers—is regarded as a significant contribution to modern poetry. Keats' acute perception of nature, art, and love, along with the sensory richness in his poetry, has made him a major influence on later poets such as Tennyson, Yeats, and Eliot.

critic.zh: 批评者指出济慈的诗歌存在过度感伤和自我沉溺的倾向，认为他过于关注个人情感而缺乏社会关怀。一些评论家认为他的作品缺乏思想深度，过分依赖华丽的意象和修辞。此外，济慈的早逝使他未能发展出更加成熟和完整的诗歌风格，他的作品在形式和结构上有时显得松散。批评者还指出，济慈对古典文学的模仿有时显得刻意，缺乏原创性。然而，这些批评往往忽视了济慈在有限生命中所达到的艺术成就，以及他对后世诗歌的深远影响。
critic.en: Critics point out that Keats' poetry tends toward excessive sentimentality and self-indulgence, arguing that he focused too much on personal emotions while lacking social concern. Some commentators believe his works lack intellectual depth and rely excessively on ornate imagery and rhetoric. Additionally, Keats' early death prevented him from developing a more mature and complete poetic style, and his works can sometimes appear structurally loose. Critics also note that his imitation of classical literature sometimes seems deliberate and lacks originality. However, these criticisms often overlook the artistic achievements Keats reached within his limited lifespan and his profound influence on subsequent poetry.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，济慈被定义为英国浪漫主义运动的核心人物，一位早逝的天才诗人。他的生平故事，特别是与范妮·布朗的爱情和最终在罗马的病逝，已成为文学浪漫主义的象征。济慈的诗歌，尤其是他的颂歌，被视为英国文学的经典之作。在流行文化中，济慈的形象常常与青春、才华和悲剧命运联系在一起，他的墓碑铭文'姓名写在水上'已成为文学不朽的象征。现代学者重视济慈对诗歌语言的革新，以及他如何将个人体验转化为普遍艺术的能力，这些都使他成为文学史上不可忽视的重要人物。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Keats is defined as a central figure of the British Romantic movement and a prodigious poetic genius who died young. His life story, particularly his love affair with Fanny Brawne and his eventual death in Rome, has become a symbol of literary romanticism. Keats' poetry, especially his odes, is regarded as classic works of English literature. In popular culture, Keats is often associated with youth, talent, and tragic fate, and his epitaph 'name writ in water' has become a symbol of literary immortality. Modern scholars value Keats' innovation in poetic language and his ability to transform personal experience into universal art, making him an indispensable figure in literary history.

self.en: 'Beauty is truth, truth beauty,'—that is all Ye know on earth, and all ye need to know.
